TutorRoster uses a light, calm visual system designed for a keyboard-first workflow: a white brand header, a quiet off-white canvas, rounded information cards, restrained colour accents, and one prominent command entry point.

The implementation lives in [`DesignSystem.css`](https://github.com/AY2627S1-CS2103T-F14-2/tp/blob/master/src/main/resources/view/DesignSystem.css). FXML defines structure and semantic component classes; the stylesheet owns colours, typography, spacing, borders, states, and control treatment.
1. **Keep the roster quiet.** The student list is the main work surface, so backgrounds and borders should be subtle.
2. **Use teal for action and orientation.** The brand colour identifies the product, primary actions, focus states, and selected records.
3. **Make information scannable.** Names are the strongest text, contact details are secondary, and addresses are tertiary.
4. **Keep the CLI visible.** The command bar is persistent and visually prominent without competing with the roster.
5. **Prefer semantic classes.** Use classes such as `person-card`, `primary-button`, and `result-display` instead of styling arbitrary nodes by position.

JavaFX does not support CSS custom properties, so these values are documented at the top of `DesignSystem.css` and repeated in the relevant component rules. Update the token comment and every corresponding rule when changing the palette.

The preferred typeface is `Helvetica`, with `Segoe UI` as the Windows fallback and the platform sans-serif font as the final fallback. Regular weight is the default; only page and dialog headings use bold weight.

Only page and dialog headings, and running indices, use bold weight. All other interface text uses regular weight; hierarchy comes from size, spacing, and colour.
Use the spacing rhythm `4, 8, 12, 16, 24, 28, 32 px`. Cards use a 14 px radius, outer shells use a 16 px radius, and compact controls use an 8–9 px radius. Prefer whitespace over extra borders.
Use `.app-shell` on the root `VBox`. Put branding and menus in `.top-bar`, main content in `.content-area`, the command entry in `.command-region`, and the file-status line in `.status-region`.
Wrap a list in `.roster-surface`. Each custom list-cell should render a `.person-card`. A card contains:
- `.card-meta` for phone and optional email; and
- `.card-detail` for the ordered subjects and education level when present.
The list view must remain transparent so the roster shell supplies the visual boundary. Do not reintroduce alternating dark row colours.

Use `.primary-button` for the one main action in a view. The command bar uses it for `Run command`; the help window uses it for `Copy URL`. The stylesheet already provides hover, pressed, disabled-compatible, and focus-visible treatment. Avoid inventing a second teal button style.

Use `.command-region` around a `.command-box`. Put the text field inside the command box and let it grow horizontally. Use the prompt icon class `.command-icon` and the existing `CommandBox#handleCommandEntered` action for both the text field and the button so keyboard and mouse users share one execution path.

Use `.result-surface` for the layout slot and `.result-display-shell` for the feedback container. The `TextArea` should use `.result-display`, remain read-only, and wrap text. Errors should use the existing `.error` class; its red colour is intentionally reserved for failure feedback.

### Student detail view and command completion
`ShowCommand` returns a `CommandResult` containing the selected `Person`. `MainWindow` consumes that
result and creates `StudentDetailModal`; the command itself does not alter the roster or filter.
Closing the modal or pressing `Esc` invokes `MainWindow.hideStudentDetails()`. This removes the modal
from the overlay, hides the overlay, and returns keyboard focus to the student list.
`CommandBoxLogic` owns `CommandCompletionLogic` and `CommandHistory`, keeping completion and command
recall independent of JavaFX controls. It executes submitted commands through an injected
prefixes. The completion list is UI guidance only: parsers remain the source of truth for validation.
Each `Suggestion` contains completion text, a displayed syntax guide, and a description. `CommandBox`
refreshes the popup when the input changes. Pressing `Tab` applies the first suggestion; clicking a
suggestion applies the selected suggestion and returns focus to the command box.
`CommandHistory` supports Up/Down navigation through entered commands and preserves the unfinished
draft when history browsing starts. This session command recall is separate from the model's
undo/redo history: recalling a command changes the input text without changing the roster.
`ListCommand` applies the full-roster predicate without changing history. `ClearCommand` replaces the
roster with an empty `AddressBook`; the central `LogicManager` then records and saves it like any other
roster change. `HelpCommand` returns a `CommandResult` that asks `MainWindow` to show `HelpWindow`, and
`ExitCommand` returns a result that asks the main window to save GUI settings and hide the stage. The
window-close handler follows the same preference-saving path.
`VersionedTutorRoster` stores private whole-roster snapshots and a pointer to the current state. It
starts with one snapshot of the loaded or sample roster. A successful roster change calls `commit()`;
the method removes any abandoned redo suffix and appends a copy of the changed roster. Undo and redo
restore a previous or later snapshot without appending a new one.

Inside the working model, `VersionedTutorRoster.undo()` first checks availability and restores the

The model-level state and the `ModelSnapshot` serve different purposes. The history states support

roster. The graphical interface displays the roster, while short keyboard commands do the work.
